source_text:
Fragmenta in Joannem
Jo , 3 Ἐν τούτῳ δὲ ἀνέτρεπεν αὐτὸς ὁ σωτὴρ δόγμα παράνομον.
ὑπονοούντων γάρ τινων ψυχὰς ἁμαρτανούσας ἐξ οὐρανοῦ τιμωρίας ἕνεκεν εἰς σῶμα
πέμπεσθαι καί ποτε μὲν καθ' ἑαυτὴν προϋπάρχουσαν τὴν ψυχὴν τοῦ σώματος
thought_title: The Savior overturns an unlawful doctrine
orientation: The author is introducing the fragment's comment on John 3, where Christ himself is said to overturn an unlawful doctrine.
pass_a_gloss: In this, the Savior himself was overturning an unlawful doctrine. For some people supposing that sinning souls are sent from heaven for the sake of punishment into a body, and that sometimes the soul pre-exists by itself apart from the body.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'unlawful doctrine' for this fixed term, preserving the sense of a teaching contrary to law.
The imperfect tense indicates ongoing or repeated action in the past, matching the narrative context of Christ's activity.
The genitive absolute participle conveys the idea of some people holding an opinion or suspicion, rendered literally as 'supposing'.
The glossary requires 'punishment' for τιμωρία, and ἕνεκεν is rendered literally as 'for the sake of' to preserve the causal force.
The glossary requires 'pre-existing' for this term, referring to the soul existing before the body.

pass_b_english: In this Christ himself overturned an unlawful doctrine. For some people supposed that sinning souls are sent from heaven into a body for the sake of punishment, and that sometimes the soul is pre-existing by itself apart from the body.

problems.source_quote: Ἐν τούτῳ δὲ ἀνέτρεπεν αὐτὸς ὁ σωτὴρ δόγμα παράνομον
problems.why: Missing opening clause: Christ himself overturned unlawful doctrine in this.
problems.fix: In this Christ himself overturned an unlawful doctrine. For some people supposed...

problems.quote: so that a woman can conceive only when some soul sins
problems.source_quote: ὑπονοούντων γάρ τινων ψυχὰς ἁμαρτανούσας ἐξ οὐρανοῦ τιμωρίας ἕνεκεν εἰς σῶμα πέμπεσθαι
problems.why: Added claim not in source: 'woman can conceive only when some soul sins' is interpretive expansion.
problems.fix: Remove the added clause; end at 'on account of its own sins.'
problems.ruling: 'woman can conceive only when some soul sins' has no basis in cited source words about souls sent into bodies.

edits.new: In this Christ himself overturned an unlawful doctrine. For some people supposed

edits.old: while at other times it is joined to bodies on account of its own sins—so that a woman can conceive only when some soul sins.
edits.new: while at other times it is joined to bodies on account of its own sins.

fixed: Added the missing opening clause about Christ overturning an unlawful doctrine.
Removed the interpretive expansion about a woman conceiving only when some soul sins.

problems.quote: while at other times it is joined to bodies on account of its own sins
problems.source_quote: ὑπονοούντων γάρ τινων ψυχὰς ἁμαρτανούσας ἐξ οὐρανοῦ τιμωρίας ἕνεκεν εἰς σῶμα πέμπεσθαι καί ποτε μὲν καθ' ἑαυτὴν προϋπάρχουσαν τὴν ψυχὴν τοῦ σώματος
problems.why: Source does not contain 'while at other times it is joined to bodies on account of its own sins' in this clause.
problems.fix: and that sometimes the soul is pre-existing by itself before the body
problems.ruling: Source clause ends at τοῦ σώματος; 'joined to bodies on account of sins' is not in the Greek text.

edits.old: and that sometimes the soul is pre-existing by itself apart from the body, while at other times it is joined to bodies on account of its own sins.
edits.new: and that sometimes the soul is pre-existing by itself apart from the body.

problems.quote: Destroying this error, Christ, when he was asked, said:
problems.why: The 'Destroying this error' clause and the John 9:3 quotation are absent from this source section; they belong to a later section.
problems.fix: Remove the 'Destroying this error' sentence and the John quotation from this section.
problems.ruling: Source ends at προϑπάρχουσαν; 'Destroying this error' and John 9:3 quotation are foreign insertion.

edits.old: Destroying this error, Christ, when he was asked, said: "Neither this man sinned nor his parents, but this happened so that the works of God might be revealed" (John 3).

fixed: Removed the 'Destroying this error' sentence and the John quotation, which belong to a later section and are absent from this source section.

problems.quote: sinning souls are sent from heaven into a body
problems.why: Same concept rendered as 'remains pre-existing' vs 'remaining' and 'sent from heaven' vs 'intertwined'
problems.fix: Use consistent terms: 'pre-exists' and 'is joined to'

variants.text: sinning souls are sent from heaven into a body
the soul is intertwined with bodies
the soul remains pre-existing by itself

problems.why: Punishment and sins are different concepts; reader may think two different doctrines
problems.fix: Clarify 'punishment for its own sins' throughout

variants.text: for the sake of its own sins

edits.old: and that sometimes the soul is pre-existing by itself apart from the body.
edits.new: and that sometimes the soul pre-exists by itself apart from the body.

edits.old: sinning souls are sent from heaven into a body for the sake of punishment
edits.new: sinning souls are sent from heaven into a body for punishment

fixed: Changed 'is pre-existing' to 'pre-exists' for consistency with the glossary term 'pre-existing'.
Changed 'for the sake of punishment' to 'for punishment' to align with the glossary term 'punishment' and avoid implying a separate concept from sins.

last_rejected.source_quote: καθ' ἑαυτὴν προϋπάρχουσαν τὴν ψυχὴν τοῦ σώματος
last_rejected.why: 'by itself' means alone, not 'apart from' which implies separation.
last_rejected.fix: the soul is pre-existing by itself, and sometimes of the body
last_rejected.ruling: καθ' ἑαυτὴν means 'by itself'; 'apart from the body' is a reasonable rendering of the contrast with τοῦ σώματος, not a major error.
